citation: George E.I.; McCulloch R.E.; Variable selection via Gibbs sampling; J. Amer. Statist. Assoc.; 88(423); 881-889
X_design: iid N(0;1) columns (Ex4.1 Problem 1); iid N(0;1) with one near-duplicate proxy column corr .989 (Ex4.1 Problem 2); common-factor equicorrelated Gaussian pairwise corr about .5 (Ex4.2); real-X Hald / happiness / bank data (Ex5.1-5.3)
X_detail: Ex4.1 P1: X1..X5 iid N_60(0;I) so practically uncorrelated; P2: identical except X3 replaced by X3*=X5+.15Z with Z~N_60(0;1) giving corr(X3;X5)=.989 (strong proxy; text does not say whether Y was regenerated; LS estimates reported as 'for these data'). Ex4.2: X_i=X_i*+Z for i=1..60 with X_1*..X_60* iid N_120(0;1) independent of Z~N_120(0;1) giving pairwise correlations of about .5. Intercept handled by centering (Sec 1). SSVS settings: f(gamma)=2^-p indifference prior; R=I (Ex5.2 also g-prior R proportional to (X'X)^-1; Ex5.3 both R=I and R proportional to (X'X)^-1); nu_gamma=0 in Ex4 and Ex5.1 and Ex5.3 (Ex5.2 nu_gamma=3 lambda_gamma=25); Ex4.1 tau_i=.33 c_i=10 (sigma_betahat/tau=1); Ex4.2 and Ex5.1 four settings (sigma_betahat_i/tau_i; c_i)=(1;5),(1;10),(10;100),(10;500) giving thresholds t_i;r_i=(2.4;1.7),(2.7;2.3),(2.1;3.2),(2.8;6.8); Gibbs sampler m=5000 draws (Ex4.1; Ex5.1) or m=30000 (Ex4.2; 31 s per 1000 iterations; 15.5 min per sample; Fortran on Sun Sparcstation 10) or m=10000 (Ex5.3 setting (10;100)); m not stated for Ex5.2; no burn-in discarded by recommendation (Sec 3)
p_max: 60 (Ex4.2 simulated); 5 (Ex4.1); real p=4 (Hald); 4 (happiness); 15 (bank; 16 variables incl. Y)
s0: 2 (Ex4.1: X4 and X5); 45 (Ex4.2: beta16..beta60 non-0; 15 nulls)
beta_SNR: Ex4.1: Y=X4+1.2*X5+eps i.e. beta=(0;0;0;1;1.2) (P2 same coefficients with X3 replaced by proxy X3*); Ex4.2: beta1..15=0; beta16..30=1; beta31..45=2; beta46..60=3 (all positive; blocks of 15 in index order); SNR or R^2 not stated; sigma used directly; LS sigma-hat 2.58 (P1) and 2.59 (P2)
replicates: single simulated dataset per problem (no replication); one Gibbs chain per tuning setting; 4 tuning settings in Ex4.2
metrics: frequency of visited gamma (top 4-5 models tabulated: Table 1 and Table 2); false choice counts (false inclusion for variables 1-15; false exclusion for 16-60); number of distinct models visited (25723;22468;5071;1901 out of 2^60) and models visited only once (23384;19390;2171;511); J-shaped frequency distribution (Fig 2); real data model frequencies (Tables 3 and 6); marginal inclusion probabilities across six priors (Fig 4); R^2; model size; Cp; no FDR/TPR/MSE reported
competitors: none in the simulations (SSVS tuning settings compared against each other only); Ex5.1 and Ex5.3 compared informally against conventional procedures: all-subsets regression; backward elimination; forward selection; stepwise; Cp; R^2

code_data: not stated (Fortran used; no code or data availability statement; Hald data cited to Draper and Smith 1981; happiness and bank data described only in text)

citation: Rockova V.; George E.I.; EMVS: the EM approach to Bayesian variable selection; J. Amer. Statist. Assoc.; 109(506); 828-846
X_design: AR1(rho=0.6) Gaussian (Sec 4-5 illustrative); equicorr(rho=0.8 within 3 groups of 33; zero between) Gaussian (Sec 7.3); real-X+real-y (yeast cell-cycle motif counts; Sec 8)
X_detail: Sec 4 (p831): rows of X ~ N_p(0;Sigma) with Sigma_ij=0.6^|i-j|. Sec 7.3 (p839): p=99 normal predictors in three equicorrelated groups {x1..x33};{x34..x66};{x67..x99} pairwise corr 0.8 within group and 0 between. Sec 8 (p841): X=counts of occurrences of each of p=4^7/2=8192 length-7 DNA motifs (reverse complement merged) in promoter of each of n=1568 genes; MRF graph: motifs differing by at most one letter joined; 8192x8192 smoothing matrix with 144896 nonzero entries (nonzero elements of theta2 set to 0.83 following Li and Zhang 2010). Prior settings: conjugate spike-and-slab with IG(nu/2;nu*lambda/2) nu=1 lambda=1 (p829); Sec 4 v1=1000 fixed; beta-binomial theta~U(0;1); EM start beta0=1_p and sigma0=1; v0 grid {0.01+k*0.01;k=0..50} (51 values). Sec 7.3: v1 given prior (6.3) with a=0.5 b=250 (mode 100); v0 grid {0.01+k*0.05;k=0..10}; start beta0 = ridge solution (5.3) with v0=1 v1=1000. n: 100 (Sec 4-5 illustrative; Sec 7.3 structured); real n=1568 genes (Sec 8)

replicates: single simulated dataset (not replicated) in Sec 4-5 and Sec 7.3; DAEMVS Table 1 varies only random starting vectors (one draw per setting); EMVS deterministic so reproducible; MH run once per setting
metrics: posterior-mode regularisation path over v0 grid (51 values; Fig 2a); log g0(gamma) of models along the path (Fig 2b; correct model {1;2;3} attains largest; Fig 4b); iterations to EM convergence (4 iterations; Sec 4); iterations to convergence and number of selected variables and log g0 (Table 1; 3 starts x 3 v0 x EMVS/DAEMVS t=0.2;0.1); Sec 7.3 TP/FP/FN/TN counts of best-visited model (BB: 21 TP 12 FN 2 FP at v0=0.21; logistic: 22 TP 11 FN 0 FP at v0=0.36; MRF: all 33 TP zero FP zero FN); MH acceptance rate 0.0001 and 50000 iterations in equal wall time; real data: selected motifs (18 at v0=9.001; 7 at v0=20.001; 4-motif best MRF model; Table 2) and run times (107 s per iteration BB; 210 s MRF; 21.4 and 17.5 min; median iterations 12 and 5)
competitors: MH stochastic search (one-step random-scan proposal) on marginal posterior of gamma with v0=0; v1=1000 (also 1;10;100); inits gamma0=0 and gamma0=full model (Sec 4.3); DAEMVS vs EMVS (Sec 5); Bernoulli fixed theta=0.5 vs beta-binomial (Sec 4); beta-binomial vs independent-logistic vs MRF priors within EMVS (Sec 7.3 and 8); Li and Zhang 2010 MCMC > 12 hr via personal communication (Sec 8); no LASSO/SCAD/other penalised comparisons
real_datasets: Yeast cell-cycle transcription-factor motif data (Spellman et al 1998; Li and Zhang 2010): n=1568 genes; p=8192 7-mer motifs; response=summary of 18 time-point expression by principal component scores (PC index not stated in text read); about half genes cell-cycle related
